findings.consequent: Distinction and definition of races and castes
findings.quote: The ancient Egyptians recognized four races. They were of the red race... The hue yellow symbolized the Asiatic peoples. White was the color of the peoples of the north... Black was the hue of the Negro. Following the Egyptians, the Aryans also divided mankind into these four races. In India four castes were founded upon the same distinctions.

findings.antecedent: Color in ancient architecture (Ziggurat, Temple of Nebuchadnezzar)
findings.consequent: Mystical significance, symbolizing divisions of the universe (underworld, earth, heavens, sun) and planets
findings.quote: The lowest stage of the tower was black, the uppermost red. The shrine was covered with blue glazed tile, the roof with gilded metal. Wooley writes, 'These colors had mystical significance and stood for the various divisions of the universe, the dark underworld, the habitable earth, the heavens and the sun.'

findings.antecedent: Colors (yellow, blue, white, red, black, green, purple, dun)
findings.consequent: Association with cardinal directions, geographical features, and elements in various cultures (Tibetan, Chinese, Irish, Navajo, Hopi)
findings.quote: In Tibet the world was conceived as a high mountain with four sides. To the north was yellow, to the south blue, to the east white, and to the west red... In Ancient China there were four heavenly kings who guarded the four quarters of the earth. The north guardian was black, the south guardian red, the east guardian green, and the west guardian white.

findings.antecedent: Colors (red, white, black, blue, green, yellow)
findings.consequent: Symbolism for fundamental elements (fire, water, earth, air) in ancient Indian, Greek, Jewish, and Chinese philosophies
findings.quote: Whatever they thought looked red, they knew was the color of fire. Whatever they thought looked white, they knew was the color of water. Whatever they thought looked black, they knew was the color of earth.

findings.antecedent: Colors (green, blue, white, red, yellow, gold, purple, emerald)
findings.consequent: Association with deities, religious concepts, and ritualistic attire in ancient Egypt, Greek mythology, Buddhism, and Islam
findings.quote: In ancient Egypt, the great god Osiris who represented solar divinity was associated with the color green, while his beautiful wife, Isis, represented the moon; her color was blue. The child Horus... was a white god, though sometimes depicted as red.

findings.consequent: Believed to assure harvest, protect from death, and treat diseases like smallpox, scarlet fever, sprains, sore throat, and fevers
findings.quote: To thwart smallpox, directed that everything about the room be red. Francis I was treated in a scarlet blanket for the same affliction. The children of one of the Mikados were surrounded by red in all furnishings during an attack of the disease.

findings.consequent: Believed to cure jaundice due to color association
findings.quote: Yellow cured jaundice because jaundice was yellow. In Germany the disease was attacked with yellow turnips, gold coins, saffron, and a dozen other yellowish things.

findings.consequent: Soothing effect on blood movement (ancient belief); effective treatment for pathologic jaundice in newborn infants (modern medicine)
findings.quote: Blue light soothed the movement of the blood; red light stimulated it. The clear light of morning aided nutrition... Visible blue light, for example, is today universally applied in offsetting pathologic jaundice in some newborn infants.

findings.consequent: Believed to cause sanguineous humor to move; red/yellow believed injurious to the eye
findings.quote: Thus, if one were to gaze intently at something red, one would cause the sanguineous humor to move. This is why one must not let a person suffering from nosebleeding see things of a brilliant red color.

findings.antecedent: Body painting with red, white, black, brown, ashes
findings.consequent: Used in aboriginal and tribal rituals for revenge, protection, and signifying status after killing
findings.quote: Painted red from head to foot... he was a demon of terror to those he sought... In Africa, similar practices were common among various tribes. The Nandi, after killing the member of another tribe, painted one side of his body, spear, and sword red, and the other side white.

findings.antecedent: Colors (red, yellow, green, blue, purple, brown, black, white)
findings.consequent: Strong emotional, social, and cultural associations reflected in idiomatic language (e.g., red for passion/danger, yellow for cowardice, blue for sadness, white for purity/peace)
findings.quote: Red is the passionate and ardent hue of the spectrum, marking the saint and the sinner, patriotism and an-archy, love and hatred, compassion and war... Yellow he despises. Rarely does he use it with any joy or munificence in his heart... Blue, however, is indispensable. It would be difficult to surpass the simple statement, 'I feel blue!'
